rationale: The candidate reads as a single dominant mass with a coherent carved/terraced subtraction, and it remains legible in all four views. It is not ideal, because the stepped/cut geometry is somewhat arbitrary and the roof/section do not yet fully express a strong programmatic span or daylight logic. Still, the form does respond to the parcel and the access edge with a visible open-ground condition rather than a sealed box, and there are no obvious inter-view collisions or severe fragmentation. For neighborhood living/mixed-use, the mass is plausible: compact, capacity-aware, with a public threshold and a calm upper body.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: Compact massing with a carved interior/open-top condition can keep a single dominant body while giving the building a public void.

reference_assessments.mismatch_warning: Office-tower language is only partially relevant; avoid over-verticalizing a neighborhood-living mass.
reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A calm primary volume with subtle taper or sectional modulation can preserve hierarchy across views.

reference_assessments.transferable_principle: A low street-responsive base with a distinct active edge and a secondary vertical marker supports neighborhood-scale mixed use.
